decision: Supporting static assessment only. Authority is only the separately recorded maintainer decision in action-risk-review.json, bound to the complete exact scope and at most 14-day validity. On 2026-10-01 agalwood authorized corrective revisions until the first formal Release succeeds in response to the disclosed .4 scope and unchanged 42 residual advisories through 2026-10-15 UTC. This fresh record binds only v9.0.2-motrix.6, not another tag or unknown new risk. Formal .5 run 36848365270 passed six candidate builds, four independent rebuilds, all secret-free approvals/final grants and both Windows final packaging jobs. After a human macOS Environment confirmation, both signers failed closed at strict MAC_CERTS Base64 decoding before PKCS12 import, code signing or notarization. Credentials were available to that step; no Secret value was inspected or Release published. Wrapped Base64 is a possible cause, not a confirmed diagnosis of the Secret. The .6 correction removes only ASCII space, tab, CR and LF from bounded raw input; canonical standard Base64, padding, nonempty data and a 64 KiB bound remain mandatory. Invalid encodings produce a generic redacted error with no partial decoded output. Tests execute the actual inline signing pipeline on public fake fixtures under isolated system Python, including negative encodings, padding, raw bounds and poisoned module paths. Both native macOS required CI and secret-free pre-sign jobs execute these tests before candidate download/approval. Certificate identity, unique Developer ID import, internal Team/certificate pins, hardened runtime, timestamp and exact ZIP notarization checks are unchanged. The prior isolated Windows packaging correction and all native fresh packaging checks remain. No Action commit, source archive/URL, toolchain, dispatch input, API binding, cache prefix, Secret name/surface, signing environment, or publication authority changes. All 42 same-day inventoried advisories remain, including cache extraction/service risks before validation and signature type-binding risk; no vulnerability is claimed fixed or wholly unreachable. Publication is conditional on every exact-commit CI check, size/race/hash/byte-comparison guard, independent rebuild, platform signing/notarization, Ed25519 root, independent final verification, fresh protected-Environment confirmation and Immutable Releases requirement. All five prior tags remain immutable, and the .5 Environment approval is not reused. New advisories, deadline extensions or unrelated source/Action updates require a new decision. This assessment itself grants no release or Environment approval.
limitations: Static call-path review, not complete dynamic taint analysis, exploit testing, or proof of non-reachability.
The lock inventory includes code beyond the selected entrypoint; findings are retained rather than suppressed.
No known advisory is considered fixed by hash verification, isolated runners, or documentation.
This assessment must be rechecked on Action, workflow, source lock, or advisory changes; it does not authorize publication.

Source-cache prefix fallback admits older same-target/runner-OS source locks. Cache bytes are not trusted, must match current archive hashes and FFmpeg PGP authentication, and never include compiled/signing inputs. Service/extraction vulnerabilities can act before those checks and remain residual risks.

glob_patterns.assessment: Trigger patterns are controlled by the protected workflow, not supplied by release users. This is a bounded-input inference, not proof that vulnerable code is absent.
controls: Download calls select exact names or run-bound numeric artifact IDs; no download pattern input is used.
Upload/cache paths and attestation globs are fixed short patterns or use the six validated target identifiers; no attacker-provided braces, extglobs, ranges, or repeated GLOBSTAR patterns.
Any workflow pattern or input-origin change invalidates this assessment.
glob_patterns.residualRisk: Globbing code is present and called. A compromised workflow or an unreviewed dynamic pattern could trigger CPU, stack, or memory exhaustion.

xml_service_messages.assessment: The vulnerable XML parser/builder is in the bundled Azure SDK; it must not be dismissed as an optional package. Artifact payload bytes are transported as a stream, not intentionally parsed as XML by this workflow. Service error/response parsing remains a possible entry path.
controls: Artifact service URLs originate from the authenticated current-run Actions service, not a dispatch URL input.
The workflow does not render parsed XML into HTML, execute it as code, or use it to authorize a release.
TLS and service integrity, exact artifact bindings, independent rebuilds, and subsequent release revalidation remain required; these do not make the XML parser safe.
xml_service_messages.residualRisk: A malicious service/proxy response could reach XML processing and cause denial of service or altered parsed fields before payload revalidation. Hash checks cannot protect credentials or code already executing in an Action. Hosted-service/TLS trust is an assumption, not a vulnerability fix.

lodash_helpers.assessment: Bundled lodash retains vulnerable helpers. The reviewed Action entrypoints do not intentionally compile user-controlled templates or call unset/omit with user-controlled array paths. Static source inspection is not exhaustive dynamic reachability proof.
controls: No dispatch-provided template, imports object, or lodash path input exists.
Any dependency call-path change or new user-controlled JavaScript object processing requires reassessment.
lodash_helpers.residualRisk: Template-import injection can execute code if an overlooked or future path admits untrusted import keys; prototype pollution may influence other consumers. No exception can be justified by artifact hashing alone.

http_optional_features.assessment: Bundled Undici includes vulnerable WebSocket, cookie, retry, and low-level HTTP paths. Reviewed Action source uses HTTPS APIs and artifact streams, not a WebSocket service or downstream HTTP proxy. Definitions in the bundle alone do not prove a reachable call.
controls: No workflow-supplied WebSocket endpoint, cookie API input, blob-like object, upgrade header, or raw duplicate Content-Length array is accepted.
API and storage destinations come from GitHub/runner services; no custom external artifact repository or run is selected.
Cookie serialization and retry-to-downstream forwarding are not workflow features; arbitrary proxy environment configuration would require a new review.
http_optional_features.residualRisk: Underlying HTTP clients are active. A compromised runner/service/proxy or an overlooked bundled call may violate these assumptions. Network timeouts do not repair protocol parsing, cookie injection, or memory-exhaustion bugs.

ip_proxy_helpers.assessment: ip-address is bundled in SOCKS/proxy support. This workflow does not implement an SSRF allowlist using its classification/subnet functions or accept a user-provided address. SOCKS/proxy processing is conditional, not demonstrably absent.
controls: Hosted runner network/proxy environment is a trusted input, not a dispatch parameter.
No arbitrary SOCKS proxy or address-classifier authorization is configured in this workflow.
ip_proxy_helpers.residualRisk: If proxy configuration or an overlooked call admits unbounded addresses, parsing may exhaust memory; NAT64, cross-family, and link-local classification errors are not repaired. Do not reuse this library as an executable-download URL allowlist.

csv_columns.assessment: csv-parse is bundled in attestation checksum-input support. This workflow supplies subject-path, not subject-checksums. No CSV columns/group-columns options are configured by the workflow.
controls: Both attestation invocations use protected static subject-path globs; SBOM is JSON.
Admitting checksum CSV or column-name objects requires a fresh review.
csv_columns.residualRisk: The package remains vulnerable if the columns path is enabled elsewhere or in a later Action. This is an input-path limitation, not a general prototype-pollution fix.

dsse_payload_type.assessment: The vulnerable preAuthEncoding function is present and used for actual signatures. The bundled attestation signer fixes the payload type to the ASCII application/vnd.in-toto+json. This prevents caller-selected types here, but does not repair the DSSE type-binding weakness.
controls: Treat provenance bundle payloadType and in-toto predicate types as exact constants during verification; do not rely on a permissive affected verifier.

Local gh 2.97.0 uses sigstore-go 1.2.2: Envelope.Statement rejects any payloadType other than application/vnd.in-toto+json; its go-securesystemslib 0.11.0 PAE uses byte-preserving Go strings and byte lengths. This is source inspection of the local version, not proof about every runner or future client.
Pinned Ed25519 manifest verification and exact repository/workflow/subject digests remain independent mandatory release checks.
Do not claim this issue is unreachable, fixed, or harmless. A maintainer must specifically review signature type-binding risk before any exception.
dsse_payload_type.residualRisk: An attacker can change payloadType to certain non-ASCII strings without changing PAE bytes for an affected verifier. Provenance integrity claims must be qualified until signer and verification behavior are reviewed or upstream fixed.
